senses.gloss:
Deoghar
(‘the होउसे of God’)
------------------------------------------
Deoghar—corrupted form of Devagṛha (‘house of God’)—is a town situated in the Santhal Parganas of the Jharkhand State. It is famous for its temple of वैद्यनाथ or Baidyanāth (Śiva), one of the twelve ज्योतिर्लिङ्गस् (See JYOTIRLIṄGAS.). Other names by which it was known are: Harītakīvana, Ketakīvana, Rāvaṇavana, Citābhūmi and Hārdapīṭha. Probably it was a forest of trees of inknuts (harītakī) or fragrant screwpine flowers (ketakī).
देओघर्">Vaidyanātha Temple at DeogharAccording to the local legends, when रावण got the शिवलिङ्ग from शिव Himself to be taken to लङ्का, the gods contrived to get it fixed to the ground on the way itself. This place has now become the present वैद्यनाथ.
This is also the place where the हृदय or the heart of सती’s body (cut by विष्णु, by his discus) is said to have fallen. Hence the name Hārdapīṭha (seat of the heart of सती), one of the 52 शक्तिपीठस् (places of शक्ति or the Divine मोथेर्).
The temple of वैद्यनाथ शिव is a simple structure with a pyramidal tower 26.5 metres (72 feet) in height. It faces east. The लिङ्ग is cylindrical in form. It is 10 cms (4 inches) high. The diameter is 12.7 cms. (5 inches). The top of the लिङ्ग is uneven.
There are different porches, some containing pillars and hanging bells.
Near the main entrance there is a well called Candrakūpa (‘well of चन्द्र or the मोओन्’). It is said to contain the essence of all the holy rivers and lakes.
A little away is the Śivagaṅgā—a large tank measuring 270 metres by 180 metres (900 feet by 600 feet)—with an embankment. It is also called Mānas-sarovar.
The rituals followed in the temple are very simple, like bathing the लिङ्ग with water, smearing with sandal paste and offering बिल्व leaves as also flowers.
There are pilgrims who bring water from the गङ्गा near Badarīnāth or even the Mānas-sarovar (in Tibet) just to bathe this लिङ्ग.
Persons suffering from serious ailments or with unfulfilled desires observe certain simple vows as lying on the bare ground and drinking the holy water with which the लिङ्ग has been bathed. They observe it for three days. The redemption is believed to come with revelations during a dream.
There are eleven other shrines in the courtyard of the temple dedicated to deities like लक्ष्मी-नारायण, पार्वती, Kālī, गणेश, सरस्वती, राम and others.
If the present temple of वैद्यनाथ was renovated or rebuilt in A. D. 1596 by one Pūraṇ Mal, the others have come up during the period A. D. 1630 to 1813, built by several others.
